claims.text: Replacing TOR-TILD's EAM reference with a DNN potential trained on ab initio solid and liquid configurations will improve reference-target phase-space overlap.
Replacing the EAM reference with the DNN potential will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
The target materials are multicomponent high-entropy alloys with five or more principal elements.
The proposed DNN should be trained on ab initio data extensively sampling liquid and near-melting configurations.
DNN potentials can describe both solid and liquid states of a high-entropy TiZrTaHfNb carbonitride near melting.
Equiatomic TiZrTaHfNb-derived refractory systems are representative high-melting candidates for the proposed method.
A DNN trained on a broad configuration set will map the alloy free-energy landscape more accurately than an EAM reference.
The DNN will better capture many-body interactions in the ab initio liquid.
The DNN will better capture configurational entropy in the ab initio liquid.
A DNN covers a more diverse range of atomic environments than an EAM potential.
Better coverage of atomic environments reduces discrepancies between the reference and ab initio target systems along the integration path.
The DNN reference may improve thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by more than 30% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM reference.
The intervention will be most effective in high-melting, compositionally complex alloys.
Traditional EAM potentials fail to capture the many diverse atomic configurations of the liquid state in these alloys.
The intervention's performance in lower-melting or less compositionally complex systems remains untested.
Prior DNN work on high-entropy carbonitrides supports the feasibility of sampling structurally distinct solid and liquid states.
A reduction of less than 30%, or one within measurement error, would falsify the proposed improvement.
